findings.summary: The proposed v2 contract does not compose with the existing snapshot-v2 contract, and the claimed shared #72 schema does not exist.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:126-145 assigns ReplicaRef and inserts a UUID before Hello's token under flaminio-repl/2, saying these bytes/fields match #72. Reviewed 72/spec.md Terms and 72/design.md Contracts/capacity-contracts.md instead define one node store, Node.capacity=72, and explicitly no replication-wire changes or ReplicaRef. Reviewed 51/contracts.md:160-200 defines HelloV2 tag0x10 with a u16 version followed by the unchanged existing Hello fields, snapshot-specific request tags and existing replies. The two v2 descriptions do not specify a common Hello/Fenced layout or which profile accepts the other's tags. 52/design.md:60-62 and 58/wire-contracts.md:28-32 also consume a nonzero store_generation that #61 declares but never defines operationally.
findings.fix: Make the dedicated identity plan the explicit owner of one concrete ref/generation schema and a composed replication profile: exact HelloV2/Fenced tags and bytes, snapshot operations when enabled, rejection/cross-decode rules, and generation initialization/change/CAS semantics. State which implementation landing second adds each hook and golden/interoperability vector. Keep the reviewed dependency plans read-only and remove the false claim that #72 already supplies these contracts. Preserve historical Q2 approval while marking the revised contract unapproved.

findings.summary: Full-response admission is left as future coordination even though the new repeated refs materially invalidate the current bound.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:126-129 adds full node+UUID nested messages for replicas, ISR, two move endpoints and releases while retaining old node projections; :146-147 only says to include them and tighten caps if needed. 80/design.md Admission and metadata bounds fixes a specific 4MiB B(N,R); 13/design.md Releases already revises it to 4160+N*(288+264*(R+1)+132), and 51/design.md Budget further accounts for snapshots/encryption. A maximal ReplicaRef alone contains a 128-byte node plus a 36-byte UUID, repeated across all these sets. Neither a numerical combined bound/caps nor treatment of formerly admitted maximum volumes is specified.
findings.fix: Derive the exact conservative combined Create/Get/Attach and relevant new-RPC budgets now, including whether legacy projections are emitted, ref/fence/release cardinalities, current #13/#51 additions, nested overhead and token/frame sizes. Publish per-RF caps and exact boundary/over-bound real Go/Rust interop fixtures under unchanged receive limits. Specify maintenance handling for existing volumes that exceed the new representation bound; do not silently make formerly supported clusters unmigratable. Assign the last-landing implementation the concrete admission/fixture hooks.

findings.summary: The #13 cleanup conversion lacks the identity-bearing contracts and transaction-bound adjustment needed to prevent confirming another disk's cleanup.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:85-90 correctly retains oldRef releases, but :124/:148 merely asks the #13 sweep/release/tombstone adapters to use exact refs. Only ChunkMeta.released_refs is assigned; no Header.Fenced/tombstone/ref confirmation fields or changed ListReleases/ConfirmRelease/ListTombstones/ConfirmDeletion contracts are given. Reviewed 13/design.md Releases uses node strings, ConfirmRelease(node,volume,chunks), Header.Fenced []string, and 118 chunks+header+ledger=120 worst-case operations. 61/design.md:59 adds a replica-gate write to every release transition, making that existing maximum 121 operations. #13's own-node io authorization cannot distinguish an old disk from the replacement on that node by itself.
findings.fix: Specify exact stored/proto/CLI/sweep contracts for ref-bound releases, fence holders and tombstones, including opened-store verification before destructive work/confirmation, old-store-return behavior and retained-reference limits. Recompute each compare/op bound (the worst ConfirmRelease write batch becomes at most117 with this added gate) and list every writer that bumps replica-gate, including cleanup/forget/deletion composition. Add both-backend max-bound and same-node wrong-UUID confirmation tests, and explicit last-landing #13/#72 hooks.

findings.summary: Same-node replacement bypasses #72's capacity admission and leaves capacity observations unbound to the store that reported them.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:73-77 describes ReplaceReplicaStore as a chunk/header/ref CAS with no capacity report, Room check or ledger change. Reviewed 72/design.md Charging and release and capacity-contracts.md charge every new move destination under a ledger compare, retain lost/released copies until exact cleanup, and expose node-keyed reports without store UUID. A replacement can therefore allocate an additional full copy without its charge; changing observed_store_uuid at 61/design.md:25-28 also leaves an old store's alive/capacity report eligible for the new store. A differently sized replacement can inherit the old disk's admission budget.
findings.fix: Define the replacement transaction's Room/ledger/charge semantics, preserving conservative charges for inaccessible old refs and snapshot multiplicity when #51 is active. Bind reports and report acceptance to the observed UUID/generation, invalidate old-store reports atomically on identity change, and reject delayed old-store heartbeats. State last-landing hooks for #72 rather than introducing a second capacity authority. Test replacement versus create/move/InitCapacity/release races and the larger-old/smaller-new disk case on both backends.

findings.summary: The simulator proof does not yet define executable checks and caught mutants for all newly introduced recovery rules.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:152-165 groups broad scenarios and explicitly names only identity_alias and bootstrap-old-token, then says every identity rule will get a check/bypass. Actual ReplicaCore::handle (replica.rs:173-199) takes Hello straight to fencing, the simulator precreates chunks (sim/mod.rs:395-401), and crash retains durable state (:1107-1121). There is no specified pure bootstrap authorization/fence-completion state or independently checked oracle for the new same-node replacement/full-resync/join transition. An identity-alias counterexample does not demonstrate rejection of dirty-only replacement, early UUID binding/join or replayed authorization after an epoch/ref change.
findings.fix: Give the sans-I/O bootstrap and replacement transitions concrete events/state/actions, including authorization completion, durable-fence completion, cancellation and chunk roles. Map each new safety rule to its independent simulator assertion, a named violating mutation, and the bounded scenario that must catch it. At minimum separate identity/ack/lease isolation, current-authority bootstrap, full-range-before-join, current-epoch/version replacement and no-authoritative-source refusal. Name real production adapter tests for both accepted remote and synthetic local Hello paths, delayed callbacks, fast-read admission/completion and restart boundaries.

findings.summary: The approved enrollment policy has no implementable migration/activation API or durable concurrency contract.
findings.evidence: 61/design.md:100-112 specifies administrator enroll-store, CAS batch cursors, inventory generation and activation, but Files and contracts names no enrollment RPC, persistent schema/keys, request/response, authorization/error rules, batch bound or activation linearization condition. Current meta/service/auth.go only recognizes enumerated RPCs, while current KV supplies ordinary Get/List/Txn APIs. The conceptual maintenance stop does not define how a resumed migration distinguishes inventories or proves every assignment/fence/release/tombstone was converted before identity-required mode resumes. The historical Q1 decision settles provenance policy, not these missing mechanisms.
findings.fix: Define the administrator-only enrollment and activation contracts with bounded batches, exact inventory/operation identity, conditional revisions, durable cursor/idempotency, conflict and lost-reply behavior, quarantine representation, and the complete activation predicate. Explain how interrupted migration and concurrent/new io registration are handled under the maintenance barrier. Add real memory/etcd restart/concurrency and auth-matrix tests; preserve the historical administrator-evidence decision without claiming these new details were already approved.
